finding.description: An extra, disconnected thumb suddenly appears on the lower left side of the phone screen and then slides down out of frame.
The text and numbers on the phone screen continuously morph, change layout, and update without any corresponding swiping or typing actions from the user.
The user's thumb makes tapping motions on the screen, but the interface does not react to these specific inputs; instead, the text continues its independent morphing.

The person walking away in the background is initially carrying a large red accessory in their left hand. As they move onto the flat path, the accessory vanishes entirely from their hands without being dropped.
The background person transitions from being midway down the stairs to several feet away on the flat pavement in a fraction of a second, resulting in a sudden, impossible jump in position.
As the right thumb moves to tap the bottom right portion of the screen, the thumb appears to clip through the solid black edge/bezel of the smartphone.
The red bag being carried by the person in the background suddenly vanishes from their hand. There is no visible action of dropping it or handing it off; the object simply ceases to exist.

verdicts.reason: At 00:06, a disconnected, thumb-like shape suddenly appears floating over the bottom left of the phone screen and then slides downward out of view.
Throughout the focus on the phone screen, the text 'A742' and other interface elements continually morph, jitter, and change layout without any corresponding user input.
Between 00:06 and 00:08, the user's right thumb makes tapping and swiping motions on the screen, but the interface does not respond to these inputs, continuing to morph independently.
The person walking down the stairs at the beginning is holding a red bag. By 00:01, as they reach the flat path, the bag completely vanishes from their hand without falling.
Between 00:00 and 00:01, the background person's walking animation glitches, causing them to unnaturally jump from the stairs to further down the flat path in an instant.
At 00:07, as the right thumb moves across the screen to tap, the tip of the thumb becomes distorted and appears to melt or clip into the screen and bezel.
This describes the same anomaly as F4. The red bag held by the background person suddenly disappears around 00:01 without being dropped.
